caption: City or regional identity logo reference with a compact modular wordmark made from rounded square blocks, bright blue, green, orange, yellow and pink color units, simple geometric cutouts, bilingual Chinese and romanized naming, and generous white negative space. Shows horizontal and stacked logo lockups for a friendly public-place brand system.
positive_aesthetic_notes: rounded modular blocks create a soft civic identity without decorative clutter
color units are bright but separated by a stable geometric grid
two lockup formats show scalable identity behavior
negative_failure_notes: do not copy the exact wordmark or city name
avoid candy-color chaos without block logic
do not add mascot illustrations or extra landmark icons
text_accuracy_notes: Use exact public names only when supplied by the user. Treat small Chinese and romanized text as reference for bilingual hierarchy, not reusable copy.
layout_notes: Large white field, compact logo cluster, stacked and horizontal lockups, wordmark aligned under or beside the symbol.

caption: Public identity system board showing a dynamic geometric logo built from green and purple rectangular tiles, white diagonal cuts, grid construction diagrams, horizontal and vertical lockups, bilingual naming, and brochure or booklet applications. The identity uses repeatable modular strips and strict measurement guides.
positive_aesthetic_notes: dynamic grid system shows how one logo grammar becomes multiple lockups
green and purple contrast is energetic but disciplined by construction lines
application mockups prove the pattern can extend beyond a single logo
negative_failure_notes: do not hallucinate exact slogan text or official identity wording
avoid random diagonal stripes that are not grid-derived
do not make the guide lines visually dominant in final logo output
text_accuracy_notes: Use text only as bilingual lockup placement reference unless exact wording is provided.
layout_notes: Top half compares logo variants and construction guides; bottom half applies the pattern to printed collateral.

caption: City identity reference board centered on a faceted M-shaped mark, with many color and material variants below. The system demonstrates one geometric letter skeleton supporting polygon facets, wireframe outlines, flat black, multicolor tessellations, gradients and line-net versions while retaining a consistent city-logo silhouette.
positive_aesthetic_notes: excellent example of a flexible civic identity family from one base silhouette
faceted geometry creates depth while preserving recognizability
variant grid teaches controlled diversity without losing the parent mark
negative_failure_notes: do not copy the exact City of Melbourne mark
avoid making every variant unrelated to the base skeleton
do not overuse gradients when a flat civic mark is required
text_accuracy_notes: Official city names and existing marks are source references only; do not reproduce as new brand output.
layout_notes: Hero mark and title at top, followed by a regular grid of variant marks with consistent spacing.

caption: Minimal lettermark exploration with eight Y-like monogram variants, each built from angular folded strokes and two to three color segments. Soft shadows and a white field emphasize the mark as a clean modular logo study rather than an application board.
positive_aesthetic_notes: controlled color swapping tests identity flexibility
single angular letter skeleton keeps all variants related
white background and sparse layout prevent visual noise
negative_failure_notes: do not create unrelated monograms in the same set
avoid unnecessary shadows in final flat logo files
do not over-fragment the letter into too many tiny pieces
text_accuracy_notes: No useful text training target; use as pure mark-structure reference.
layout_notes: Two-row variant grid on a white field with even spacing and small soft shadow anchors.

caption: Municipal township logo system board with grayscale place-reference photographs, grid-based icon extraction, and six sub-identity marks derived from local architecture, gates, lakes, birds and towers. Final marks use pixel-like red and warm tan strokes with black bilingual office names below.
positive_aesthetic_notes: strong method chain from local feature photo to grid icon to township sublogo
shared red and tan palette unifies different local symbols
sub-brand grid proves how multiple towns can share one identity grammar
negative_failure_notes: do not copy exact township names or official sublogos
avoid reducing place culture to arbitrary tourist icons
do not mix too many colors when sublogos need one family identity
text_accuracy_notes: Chinese and English township names require source confirmation. Use this case mainly for derivation logic and sublogo hierarchy.
layout_notes: Top explanatory section, photo reference row, grid abstraction row, then six final sublogo lockups in a balanced grid.

view_type: commune identity master logo and sublogos
caption: Regional commune identity system with a precise construction diagram, green M-shaped line mark, black node points, tall condensed sans typography, and multiple commune sublogos using different node arrangements and green-to-lime color variations. The system combines territorial map-network logic with a consistent parent mark.
positive_aesthetic_notes: clear parent-child identity system using a common M framework
node positions encode local variation without changing the family grammar
thin line construction and condensed type create a civic contemporary tone
negative_failure_notes: do not copy exact French municipal names or official marks
avoid random dots that do not encode a sub-identity rule
do not let thin lines become fragile or unreadable at small sizes
text_accuracy_notes: Long French names are reference text only unless supplied by the user. Preserve hierarchy rather than exact copy.
layout_notes: Top construction drawing, middle master lockup, lower two-column list of sublogos and text lockups.

caption: Urban identity logo exploration using black square pixels, neon green motion blur, radial and grid arrangements, and a Taipei wordmark with pixel accents. The study shows how digital movement, city rhythm and modular pixels can become a contemporary place identity.
positive_aesthetic_notes: digital pixel grammar creates a distinct urban technology identity
green glow is functional as motion energy rather than decoration
letterform and symbol variants share black square endpoints
negative_failure_notes: do not create noisy glow or unreadable pseudo-tech effects
avoid copying exact Taipei wordmark or official identity
do not scatter pixels without a motion or grid rule
text_accuracy_notes: City name text is source reference. For new work, use exact supplied city name and verify spelling before generation.
layout_notes: Concept text on left; symbol evolution and wordmark variants arranged across a sparse white board.

caption: Creative center identity system with TNHCC abbreviation, long horizontal rules, vertical and horizontal lockups, narrow image strips, black typographic structure, and varied placements that turn the name into a horizon-like graphic system. The visual identity is strict, editorial and architecture-like.
positive_aesthetic_notes: wordmark structure becomes the graphic container for image strips
horizontal line grammar strongly supports the New Horizon concept
multiple lockups show flexible signage and editorial usage
negative_failure_notes: do not copy the exact abbreviation or institution name
avoid using random photo strips without a structural role
do not let thin horizontal lines overpower legibility
text_accuracy_notes: Institution naming is reference only. New identity prompts must supply exact abbreviation and full name.
layout_notes: Sparse gray field with several logo lockups; image strips nested into long black typographic frames.
